git commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
fix(spl): `$obj->$name()` on a builtin class had no body to reach

MEASURED: a loop over method NAMES died where php answers every one.

    $i = new SplFileInfo("f.txt");
    foreach (["getFilename", "getSize"] as $call) { $i->$call(); }

    php    : f.txt, 4
    elephc : Fatal error: callable array did not resolve to an invokable target

The same loop worked as soon as each name had ALSO been called statically somewhere
in the program. That is what said the dispatch ladder is bounded not by the names a
program mentions but by the BODIES that were emitted — the ladder skips any
candidate whose method the module never lowered.

Builtin SPL method bodies are lowered ON DEMAND, from a pass that reads the method
name out of each `MethodCall` instruction. A dynamic call carries no name there, so
the pass found nothing and the class went out with the methods it happened to need
for its interfaces and nothing else.

The pass now also widens when the module contains a run-time invoke, and the
widening is bounded by the classes the program CONSTRUCTS: a program with no
dynamic invoke pays nothing, and one that has them pays only for what it built.
`echo 1;` is unchanged at 53 760 bytes.

A USER class was never affected — its methods are lowered because the class is
declared — and that asymmetry is exactly what made this read as a dispatch bug
rather than a missing body. The user case is pinned alongside the builtin one so
widening the second cannot disturb the first.

Verified: 279 `spl::`, 1097 `io::` and 1535 unit tests pass, and the 183-program
round-8 corpus is unchanged at 180 identical.

Found while probing and left open, because it is a slot-layout question rather than
a streams one: a variable that holds an OBJECT cannot be reassigned to any other
kind, in either direction — `$v = new A(); $v = 42;` is refused at compile time with
`cannot reassign $v from A to int`, and so are string, float, bool and array, and
the reverse. Only `$v = null` is accepted. php allows all of them.
